Question
========
Consider the following piece of JSON:

```
{
  "Operator": "DVB",
  "Vehicle": "Stadtbus",
  "LineNr": "85"
}
```

Which statement correctly describes the syntax of a JSON object such as this one?

Answerlist
----------
* An object is wrapped in square brackets and contains a list of values separated by colons.
* An object is wrapped in curly brackets and contains zero or more name-value pairs; each name is a string, name and value are separated by a colon, and the pairs are separated by commas.
* An object is wrapped in curly brackets, but unlike an array it cannot contain more than three name-value pairs.
* An object never contains other objects or arrays as values, only plain strings and numbers.


Solution
========
A JSON object is delimited by a pair of curly brackets `{ }` and holds zero or more name-value pairs. Each name has to be a string, a single colon separates a name from its value, and consecutive pairs are separated by commas - exactly as shown in the example above. There is no limit on how many pairs an object may contain, and a value is free to be another object or an array, which is exactly what makes JSON suitable for nested, semi-structured data.

Answerlist
----------
* False
* True
* False
* False
